claims.claim: Eustathius was bishop of Antioch from approximately 324 to 327.
Eustathius was born at Side in Pamphylia.
Eustathius died in exile at Trajanopolis in Thrace, most probably in 360, though some sources say 336 or 337.
Eustathius was first bishop of Beroea in Syria before being transferred to Antioch.
Eustathius was deposed and exiled to Trajanopolis in Thrace around 329 or 330 by Emperor Constantine the Great due to intrigues of pro-Arian bishops.
The only complete work by Eustathius that survives is De Engastrimytho contra Origenem (Against Origen on the Woman of Endor).
The work was written almost a century after Origen's analysis of the passage of King Saul's visit to the witch of Endor in 1 Samuel 28.
Eustathius's response to Origen is purposefully critical because in his eyes Origen had tackled some of the basic principles of biblical criticism.

A new edition of De Engastrimytho, together with the respective homily of Origen, was made by A. Jahn in 1886 in Gebhardt and Harnack's 'Texte und Untersuchungen zur Geschichte der altchristlichen Literatur'.
